Starbucks, which has roughly 500 cafes in India through its joint venture with Tata Consumer Products
, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The move comes days after US pharmacy chain Walgreens signed a pact with the Tamil Nadu state government to establish a GCC in its capital Chennai, already home to tech centres of global corporates including Citi, Barclays and American Express.

GCCs have moved beyond low-cost back-office support, ​with global business groups using these centres to support headquarters through higher-value functions such as ⁠finance and software development as well as research and development.
